# Retained Argon2 0.5.3 compatibility patch

This is the public RustCrypto `argon2` 0.5.3 crate, retained under its original
MIT/Apache licenses. `UPSTREAM.json` records its registry archive checksum,
upstream revision and hashes of every retained original file. The archive hash
matches the previous root Cargo.lock. Source and known-answer tests are retained.

The first upstream source change adds `Params::new_go_legacy_memory`. Released
Go accepts encoded memory from `4 * lanes` while its Argon2 implementation fills
at least `8 * lanes` blocks. The requested memory is included in H0 **before**
that minimum is applied. Upstream `Params::new` rejects this historical range;
raising the encoded memory produces a different key and rejects genuine vaults.

The added constructor permits only `4 * lanes <= memory < 8 * lanes` with
1–16 lanes. It delegates time/output validation to the unchanged constructor,
then preserves the original memory field. Upstream hashing, compression, block
filling semantics and the standard constructor remain unchanged. Host policy reserves
the effective memory before derivation. Production write defaults stay at
64 MiB, three passes and four lanes.

The second change fills the lanes of each slice in parallel, as Go's
`x/crypto/argon2` does with goroutines (vault unlock derives with `p=4`; the
sequential upstream fill made Rust unlock about twice as slow). Argon2 only
synchronises lanes at slice boundaries: within a slice a lane writes just its
own segment and, by RFC 9106 section 3.4, never reads the current segment of
another lane. `fill_blocks` therefore keeps the pass/slice loop and moves the
unchanged per-lane body into `fill_segment`, generic over a small
`SegmentMemory` trait. Sequential fill uses the whole matrix; with the `std`
feature and more than one lane, `fill_slice_parallel` splits the matrix into
`lanes * 4` segment chunks and hands each lane (via `std::thread::scope`)
its own current chunk as `&mut` plus every chunk of the other slices as `&`;
the other lanes' current chunks are unreachable. This is safe Rust, adds no
dependency and no `unsafe`, and the output is bit-identical (lane results do
not depend on scheduling). If a thread cannot be spawned the lane is filled on
the calling thread. Without `std` (or with `p=1`) the code is sequential.
`symvault-crypto` enables `std`. Tests: `parallel_lanes_match_sequential_*`
(lib tests, block-by-block over algorithms, versions, lane counts and Go legacy
memory) and `tests/parallel_lanes.rs` (keys generated by Go
`argon2.IDKey`, including `t=3,m=65536,p=4`). `UPSTREAM.json` pins the patched
`src/lib.rs` under `local_patches`; its upstream hash stays in `original_files`.

The immutable released Go source generates and authenticates the retained
`minimum_read` identity with memory=4 and lanes=1. Both implementations must
read it with the original passphrase. Upstream known-answer tests and a source
hash guard cover the standard algorithm and limit the retained patch surface.

On a dependency update, compare all upstream changes, regenerate provenance
from the public archive, rerun upstream known answers and genuine Go historical
vectors, and update both the root and fuzz locks. Remove the legacy patch when upstream
provides an equivalent explicit compatibility constructor, and the parallel patch
when upstream fills lanes concurrently. Never replace this
with parameter rounding or a separate cryptographic implementation.
